articles.title: ‘I miss old Google’: readers tell us how they search the internet in the age of AI
articles.summary: A feature called AI Overviews has been a profound change, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting. Google has put artificial intelligence at the front and center of its search bar.
body: “AI is driving the most significant upgrade of the Google Search experience ever,” wrote Liz Reid, Google’s vice-president of search, last August. In May, the company said more AI is coming.

As people grow accustomed to AI chatbots, they’re spending more time with Google’s and therefore more time on Google.com. Academic studies are finding that people navigate less to sites beyond Google if an AI Overview can give them a good enough answer, even if the bot cites the sites that feed it. Clicks, also known as traffic, are often the most significant way a website earns money from advertising. Media outlets and website owners are enduring a sustained traffic decline. Large US media companies are suing Google, alleging that AI summaries have redirected and reduced traffic to their sites, cutting into their revenue.

Google said it had not seen a decline in aggregate traffic and that such accusations are based on “flawed methodologies”. Reid, the company’s vice-president of search, wrote last year: “Total organic click volume from Google Search to websites has been relatively stable year-over-year.”

articles.title: Italian pop legend takes the lead in Maria Grazia Chiuri’s Fendi collection
articles.summary: Milan show full of diaphanous dresses and visible bras celebrates ‘incredible feminist’ of the 1970s, Raffaella Carrà. Maria Grazia Chiuri has been having more fun with clothes since she decamped from Paris back to her native Rome to work at Fendi. “I have less of a uniform these days.
body: Not that Chiuri doesn’t approach her work as a designer seriously. She described her second ready-to-wear season at Fendi not as a show, or a collection, but as “the second part of the project I am working on for them”.

She is continuing the protocol she developed as the designer of Dior of using each event as a platform to celebrate women’s creativity. But instead of a ceramicist or a philosopher, her muse for this season is the Italian pop legend Raffaella Carrà.

Carrà, once described as a “one-woman Abba ”, had a Lady Gaga bob and a taste for sequined catsuits. She caused a sensation with her raunchy outfits – the first bare midriff ever seen on Italian TV, in 1970 – and her sex-positive lyrics (her song A Far L’Amore Comincia Tu translates as “Take the lead when making love”).
“She was an incredible feminist, and her relationship with her clothes was so free,” said Chiuri of Carrà, who died aged 78 in 2021.

articles.title: Something in your eye? Here’s how to get it out – without making it worse
articles.summary: It’s natural to want to soothe eye irritation, but mishandling could lead to more problems, experts warn. We asked them for advice on how to deal with it properly. It may feel like a gritty, annoying sensation, or a sharp pain.
body: Addressing the situation incorrectly can lead to bigger issues such as infection, scarring, an ulcer or corneal scratches, which are abrasions on the clear covering of your eye. Ignoring the dilemma can lead to similar consequences.
Experts explain how to handle this predicament, when it’s time to see a medical professional, and some of the most common mistakes.

As innocuous as they may seem, eyelashes are some of the most common foreign bodies to get stuck in eyes. If an eyelash ends up under an eyelid, it can be quite painful, explained Dr Douglas Lazzaro, an ophthalmologist and professor at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine.

Other common examples Lazzaro encounters include dust and other small debris kicked up on a windy day and glue from attaching false eyelashes. Those working in construction may encounter flecks of industrial materials such as fiberglass, metal and wood.

articles.title: The Best Fall Jackets 2026 to Shop, From Little Jackets to Suede Blazers
articles.summary: Whether straight off the runway or just in from our go-to labels, the best fall jackets are as stylish as they are sensible. Shop styles from Cos, Khaite & more.
body: Wrap up, zip up, or button up. However you go about it, the time to pull out your fall jackets is swiftly approaching. As fall settles in, that slight chill in the air—and the increasingly shorter days—are getting harder to ignore. True jacket weather is imminent, making now the perfect time to revisit the outerwear trends that walked the runways back in February as you build out your seasonal wardrobe and reacquaint yourself with the idea of layering.

The fall 2026 jacket trends are all about fresh iterations of the classics—but rather than thinking of them as the addendum to your look, make them the centerpiece. Nowhere does that sentiment resonate stronger than with the funnel-neck. In leather, denim, and even cotton, the style appeared in seemingly every collection, from Chloé and Saint Laurent to 2025 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund runner-up Stephanie Suberville of Heirlome.

articles.title: “It Takes Care And Commitment”: Stella McCartney Cosigns A New Sustainable Coalition
articles.summary: “I think people have good intentions; it’s just a big problem to solve,” says Stella McCartney, as she unpacks The Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition for Vogue.
body: There’s no doubt that sustainability has fallen down the fashion agenda in recent years, with brands increasingly concerned about their bottom lines. But now a new initiative, The Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition, hopes to reignite the conversation — and more importantly, accelerate action – when it comes to tackling the industry’s impact on the planet. More than 60 brands, retailers, manufacturers and innovators have joined so far, with each signatory committing to reaching net zero emissions by 2040.

Among the key names involved? Stella McCartney, one of fashion’s most outspoken proponents for change since launching her eponymous brand more than 20 years ago. “The conversation has been happening for a long time now,” the designer tells Vogue, speaking via Zoom from her London studio. “I think people have good intentions; it’s just a big problem to solve. [There’s] not an overnight solution, and it does take care and commitment.”

body: When it comes to the world of celebrity children, it feels like no name is too unusual. Whether the famous parents are taking inspiration from nature, the calendar, or indie rock bands, they’re choosing names that make an impression and announce their creativity.

Earlier this year, Meghan Trainor and Daryl Sabara added a new entry to the canon when they announced the birth of their daughter, Mikey Moon Trainor. And now, model Elsa Hosk and her fiancé Tom Daly have announced the birth of their second daughter, Flora Blue. Hosk and Daly join a community of celebrities who have borrowed from the color wheel when choosing a baby name.

And then there are Rihanna and A$AP Rocky, who called their first son RZA in honor of the legendary Wu-Tang Clan rapper; their second son Riot Rose; and their daughter Rocki Irish. Meanwhile, Kourtney Kardashian and Travis Barker welcomed their own baby Rocky in 2023.

articles.title: How Garmin's New 'Epic' Feature Helps Me See the Bigger Picture of My Training
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Garmin's new logging feature, Garmin Epic, is getting buried in the launch of the latest Fenix 9 watch, but it deserves a headline of its own.
body: First things first: Garmin Epics are not to be confused with Garmin's older watch line, epix, with an "x". This feature is Epic, with a "c". The names are close enough that searching for one turns up the other, so double-check the spelling.

A Garmin Epic is a digital travel journal that combines your activities, maps, photos, and key health and performance metrics into a single interactive timeline you can revisit and share. With the Fenix 9 smartwatch, you can create and start an Epic directly from your watch. For older watches, you can still create Epics in the Garmin Connect app.

Once you create an Epic, you can see all activities on one map, photos, an activity feed, daily notes, and selected performance and health reports across the whole span. It's a free Garmin Connect feature, and Garmin's launch demo showed a Reports tab with sleep score, resting heart rate, and HRV status for the same dates.
